response.rationale: Both forms naturally refer to an aircraft seat beside the aisle. Indonesian commonly uses “kursi lorong,” while Malaysian commonly uses the descriptive phrase “tempat duduk tepi lorong.”
response.risk_rationale: Airline wording may vary slightly, especially between “tepi lorong” and “lorong,” without changing the sense.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Tempat duduk lorong” may be understood in Indonesian, but “kursi lorong” is a useful Indonesian preference; the Malaysian descriptive form remains ordinary and natural there.
